keyFindings.description: release_children's started/held are read back from records the request has not written: a child released from triage/backlog/icebox (the normal path; only SetStatus todo is sent, the record arrives later with Dispatch's event) is in neither list, so a blocked one answers held: []; a parked child (record at done) released again is answered started though nothing started. Breaks spec acceptance 'the answer names the children started and the children waiting'. Reproduced with a throwaway test over the package's own releaseHarness against Postgres 17: backlog child blocked on an in_progress issue -> {"released":["LEGION-209"],"started":[],"held":[]}; parked child -> started:["LEGION-210"]. Every existing test and the driven proof set the child todo first.

No '## Contract change census': the PR makes admission.blocked and the release answer's started/held required in the plugin's strict schemas under contract 37 (a process-boundary change); INFRA-229's census convention (docs/solutions/legion/a-contract-census-...-INFRA-229.md) applies.

Free-slot formula (cap - active - waiting) and 'takes the next free slot by itself' no longer hold: slotFree now leaves blocked waiting roots out (admit.go:263-274), so the controller cannot confirm the slot-free wake the daemon sends.

Lifecycle text omits the second exemption (a tree Legion takes back after it finished and lingered starts whatever its links say; blockers.Exempt TakenBack), required by spec acceptance 59/63, and claims `legion state` reports the slot free, which the CLI does not print.

Re-pointed test now flips an existing key's value instead of adding a key the fixture lacks, so it no longer encodes 'Dispatch may add fields a deployed daemon does not read' (spec acceptance line 65).
